paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God is light, and in Him there is no darkness at all (1 John 1:5). That's the message the writer heard from Him, and it's the ground everything else in this letter stands on. So if we say we have fellowship with Him yet walk in the darkness, we lie and do not practice the truth (1 John 1:6). I know that stings a little, but a light that bright is not trying to embarrass you. It's showing you where the floor is.

Now here's the part I LOVE. We don't have to pretend. If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves (1 John 1:8), and I have been that stamper, friend, blurry edges and all, insisting I looked sharp. But if we confess our sins, "He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness" (1 John 1:9). Owning it is not the price you pay for forgiveness. It's just you stepping into the light, where the blood of Jesus His Son cleanses us from all sin (1 John 1:7).

And you're not stepping in alone. The writer says he's writing so that we will not sin, but if anyone does sin, we have an advocate before the Father, Jesus Christ, the Righteous One (1 John 2:1). He Himself is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not only for ours but also for the sins of the whole world (1 John 2:2). That's why the writer can say his joy is complete when we share this fellowship with the Father and with His Son (1 John 1:3-4). So walk in the light today, baker, and when you stumble, don't hide in the dark. Come back to the One who already covered it.
